issues.description: Name mismatch for the global compute-table variable: the template dd.py declares the compute table as `_CT = ComputeTable()`, but the template dd_simulation.py imports and uses `CT`. This will cause import/NameError issues and prevents students from running or implementing DD operations (add/multiply) as the expected compute-table API (CT.lookup / CT.insert) is unavailable. The solution repository uses `CT`, indicating the intended name is `CT` (no underscore).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the compute-table name consistent in the template. Rename `_CT` to `CT` in template/dd.py, or alternatively change the imports and usages in template/dd_simulation.py to use `_CT`. Prefer renaming `_CT` to `CT` to match the solution and the intended API (`CT.lookup`, `CT.insert`).

issues.description: The compute-table instance (ComputeTable) is named _CT in template_repository/dd.py but is imported and referenced as CT in template_repository/dd_simulation.py (and in the solution). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (the global compute table) will cause import/reference errors and confuses students about the intended global name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the compute-table variable in template_repository/dd.py from _CT to CT to match imports and usage in dd_simulation.py (or alternatively change imports/usages to _CT). Prefer using CT (no leading underscore) to align with the solution and template dd_simulation.py.
